chapters.title: What Motivates Us Really?
chapters.sourcePressure: The opening move says distraction usually starts with internal discomfort, while devices and apps are downstream channels for relief.
chapters.coreMove: Trace the impulse to the uncomfortable feeling it is trying to quiet before blaming the nearest device.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would make the phone the villain and skip the boredom, anxiety, or uncertainty that made the phone attractive.

chapters.title: Time Management Is Pain Management
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter turns the internal-trigger frame toward calendar behavior, showing that delay and respectable substitute tasks often protect the reader from discomfort.
chapters.coreMove: Treat a slipped schedule as evidence of avoided discomfort and plan the moment when that discomfort will be faced.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would teach better scheduling without naming the pain that the schedule is being used to dodge.

chapters.title: Deal with Distraction from Within
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter stays with internal triggers and moves from diagnosis toward intercepting urges before they become visible distraction.
chapters.coreMove: Catch the urge in the body, label it plainly, and create a small pause before it chooses the next action.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would tell the reader to resist urges harder instead of watching the urge long enough to separate it from action.

chapters.title: Reimagine the Internal Trigger
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter deepens the internal-trigger work by changing the meaning assigned to discomfort rather than pretending discomfort should vanish.
chapters.coreMove: Rewrite the story attached to a bad feeling so it becomes information to work with, not an order to escape.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would ask the reader to put a positive spin on discomfort instead of changing the story that gives the feeling control.

chapters.title: Reimagine the Task
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter shifts from trigger interpretation to task shaping, reducing avoidable friction without pretending serious work should feel effortless.
chapters.coreMove: Find the puzzle, choice, or visible progress inside a necessary task so escape is no longer the most interesting option.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would tell the reader to make hard work fun and skip the specific redesign that changes the task's pull.

chapters.title: Reimagine Your Temperament
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter closes the internal-trigger section by replacing fatalistic self-stories with a behavior-based view of attention.
chapters.coreMove: Stop treating distractibility as a fixed identity and choose the next behavior that proves a different self-story.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would sort people into personality types rather than loosening the identity story that grants permission to drift.

chapters.title: Turn Your Values into Time
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter opens the traction section by converting values into visible time commitments, with timeboxing as more useful than list maintenance.
chapters.coreMove: Translate a value from a belief into a protected block on the calendar that can be kept or renegotiated honestly.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would ask the reader to list priorities without forcing values to occupy actual time.

chapters.title: Control the Inputs Not the Outcomes
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter clarifies what the reader owns inside scheduled time: controllable effort and process signals, not guaranteed outcomes.
chapters.coreMove: Define success for a block by the input you can deliver, then release the outcome you cannot command.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would pretend outcomes do not matter instead of separating them from the controllable process.

chapters.title: Schedule Important Relationships
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter carries values-to-time logic into close relationships, protecting presence without measuring love by calendar volume.
chapters.coreMove: Give important people protected time before leftovers and urgent fragments consume the relationship by default.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would turn love into calendar math or generic advice to spend more quality time.

chapters.title: Sync with Stakeholders at Work
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter closes traction by protecting work time through explicit alignment with people whose expectations can otherwise become interruptions.
chapters.coreMove: Make your planned work visible to stakeholders before silence gets misread as neglect or availability.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would preach focus at work without negotiating the expectations that make focus possible.

chapters.title: Ask the Critical Question
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter opens the external-trigger section with a fast filter: does this cue serve prior intent or pull the reader away from it.
chapters.coreMove: Interrogate each external cue by asking whether it serves the thing you meant to do right now.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would treat all alerts as bad instead of judging each cue against prior intent and real obligations.

chapters.title: Hack Back Work Interruptions
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter converts trigger judgment into negotiated work norms, treating interruptions as shared-system events rather than coworker flaws.
chapters.coreMove: Make focus and interruptibility legible at work so people know when to wait, reroute, or interrupt for true urgency.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would blame coworkers instead of designing visible norms for shared attention.

chapters.title: Hack Back Email
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter narrows work-interruption logic into the inbox, treating email as a repeat trigger system that needs bounded handling and norms.
chapters.coreMove: Turn email from a constant cue into a batched commitment with clear next handling rules.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would chase inbox zero prestige or declare email evil instead of building bounded response paths.

chapters.title: Hack Back Group Chat
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter distinguishes group chat by its speed and visible-presence pressure, focusing on norms and urgency rules rather than blaming the app.
chapters.coreMove: Separate chat's coordination value from its ambient presence pressure by naming channels, urgency, and expected response speed.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would mute everything or blame chatty people without defining what the room is for.

chapters.title: Hack Back Meetings
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter treats meetings as synchronous claims on time that must earn their place through coordination design and clear purpose.
chapters.coreMove: Require a meeting to state the decision, preparation, and time claim before it consumes shared attention.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would mock meetings or advise fewer meetings without showing how a useful meeting earns its cost.

chapters.title: Hack Back Your Smartphone
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter begins the personal-device stretch by treating the smartphone as a portable trigger source that can be reconfigured without abstinence fantasies.
chapters.coreMove: Redesign the phone so useful tools remain reachable and unplanned cues lose their default path to your attention.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would demand a phone detox instead of changing the device's trigger design.

chapters.title: Hack Back Your Desktop
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter extends trigger redesign to the larger digital workspace, focusing on defaults, visibility, and switching paths.
chapters.coreMove: Arrange the desktop so the next intended action is visible and competing paths require deliberate effort.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would confuse a clean desktop with a governed desktop.

chapters.title: Hack Back Online Articles
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter narrows browser drift to article pages where links, sidebars, and recommendations turn bounded reading into wandering.
chapters.coreMove: Turn reading into a bounded act by choosing the article, capture path, and stopping point before links choose for you.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would become anti-reading advice instead of protecting intentional reading from page-level prompts.

chapters.title: Hack Back Feeds
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter intensifies browser drift by focusing on feeds as endless sequences with weak stopping cues and novelty-driven next items.
chapters.coreMove: Convert feed use from an endless default into a chosen visit with a purpose, boundary, and exit cue.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would scold social media or blame algorithms instead of building a stopping structure.

chapters.title: The Power of Precommitments
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter introduces pacts as future-facing constraints used when present-moment intention repeatedly loses.
chapters.coreMove: Make the desired future choice before temptation arrives, while the calmer self can still set the rules.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would use precommitments as punishment or as the first tool before internal triggers and traction are handled.

chapters.title: Prevent Distraction with Price Pacts
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter treats price pacts as one subtype of pact, attaching explicit consequence before the weak moment so distraction stops feeling cheap.
chapters.coreMove: Attach a meaningful cost to a clearly defined distraction only after the desired path is already planned and possible.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would make money penalties sound like a gimmick and skip the order of operations.

chapters.title: Prevent Distraction with Identity Pacts
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter treats identity pacts as a different reinforcement mechanism, tying follow-through to a chosen identity proved through action.
chapters.coreMove: Choose a concrete identity that makes the planned behavior feel like proof of who you are, not a rule you are enduring.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would drift into affirmations instead of tying identity to repeated visible behavior.

chapters.title: Fixing Distraction Is a Test of Company Culture
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter moves to workplace culture, shifting blame from individual weakness to norms, coordination, and permission systems.
chapters.coreMove: Diagnose workplace distraction by looking at the norms people are rewarded or punished for following.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would tell employees to focus harder inside a culture that punishes focus.

chapters.title: The Indistractable Workplace
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter describes operational habits of a healthier workplace built from explicit coordination, routines, and permission across channels.
chapters.coreMove: Turn attention-friendly culture into shared routines that make focused work, responsiveness, and recovery predictable.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would imagine a utopian quiet office instead of concrete shared practices people can rely on.

chapters.title: Understand Their Internal Triggers
chapters.sourcePressure: The child section applies the discomfort lens to children, asking caregivers to look for urges and uncomfortable states before blaming devices.
chapters.coreMove: Respond to a child's device pull by getting curious about the feeling underneath it before imposing a rule.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would blame screens or diagnose children rather than noticing discomfort and asking better questions.

chapters.title: Make Time for Traction Together
chapters.sourcePressure: The child section applies traction and timeboxing through shared family planning, collaboration, and prior intent rather than reactive conflict.
chapters.coreMove: Build a child's traction plan with them so important activities and free time are chosen before conflict starts.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would impose a parent-made schedule and call it responsibility.

chapters.title: Help Them with External Triggers
chapters.sourcePressure: The child section applies external-trigger shaping with adult scaffolding, helping children notice and change cues in their environment.
chapters.coreMove: Help a child spot the cue that pulls them off plan and change the environment with them instead of policing every lapse.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would hide every device or blame platforms without teaching cue awareness.

chapters.title: Teach Them to Make Their Own Pacts
chapters.sourcePressure: The child section adapts pact-making into guided self-authorship, preserving developmental limits while moving beyond imposed rules.
chapters.coreMove: Guide a child to design a small pact they understand, own, and can adjust after seeing what happens.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would make adult rules look like child-made commitments.

chapters.title: Spread Social Antibodies Among Friends
chapters.sourcePressure: The child section moves into peer norms, showing how practical social antibodies can protect attention in friendship settings.
chapters.coreMove: Help young people create small peer norms that make distraction easier to notice and harder to spread.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would moralize about bad friends instead of building practical social resistance together.

chapters.title: Be an Indistractable Lover
chapters.sourcePressure: The closing chapter synthesizes internal triggers, external triggers, traction, and pacts into relational attention and defended presence.
chapters.coreMove: Use structure to protect presence with the person you love, then let the structure disappear into actual attention.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would turn intimacy into productivity or imply systems can replace tenderness.
